findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can opener was observed with dry debris contaminating it. The PIC was shown and moved the item to dish for cleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a ready-for-use sanitizer (sani bucket) in the kitchen areas. When asked a bucket was produce at effective concentration for the kitchen that corrected the immediate violation. Ensure that a ready-for use sanitizer is available at all times that the facility is handling or preparing foods and food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

The CFPMs available for the facility had not completed the required allergen training at the time of the inspection. Education was conducted and the PIC was instructed to have the required training completed and the certificates available prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine in the bar area was tested at 0ppm. After several cycles, a bottle replacement, and priming of the machine, the concentration tested at 100ppm (CL). It appears that the chlorine bottle was empty and needed to be replaced. Additionally, the sanitizer chemical (at triple sink) in the kitchen area was also tested at 0ppm (CL). The facility uses the chemical at the dispenser to sanitize food contact surfaces. Instructed the facility to manually make the buckets until the dispenser can be serviced. Violation corrected on site. Ensure that sanitizer concentrations are always testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was a slight accumulation of dried debris on the food contact surfaces of the can opener. Shown to the owner and the can opener was placed through the dish machine to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There were several boxes of food stored on the floors of the walk in cooler and walk in freezer. Suggested purchasing metal racks (or crates) that are at least six inches from the floor to protect against contamination. Ensure that food is never stored on the floor and is at least six inches from ground level.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build-up of food debris behind the cook line. Discussed with PIC, and PIC stated that the kitchen is professionally cleaned once a month. Ancillary cleaning in-between professional cleanings may be required to keep this area clean. Ensure the cook-line equipment is cleaned behind regularly enough to keep the area clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Inspector observed an employee wash hands and use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet. He then use the same paper towel to dry hands. Employee was coached and properly washed hands. Train hand washing continually. Violation is considered corrected on site. 
(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Inspector observed the counter in the men’s restroom is no longer sealed to the par wall separating it from the urinal. Seal the counter to the wall. 
PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Ice scoop was observed in the bar ice bin with the handle in contact with the ice.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on-site.  Ensure ice scoops are stored with the hand out of the ice to prevent contamination.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need of caulk:
-Kitchen hand sink
-Bar hand sink
Ensure these areas are sealed to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket measured 10 ppm (cl) at time of inspection.  Discussed with PIC and discovered the sanitizer dispenser was not working properly.  PIC removed a part in the line that controls the flow of the sanitizer, in which the sanitizer is now measuring 200 ppm.  When mixing sanitizer buckets and the filling the 3 part sink, add water to dilute to 100 ppm.  Ensure sanitizer concentration is checked periodically for proper sanitation.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Freshly prepped fish was observed in the prep cooler without date marking.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on-site.  Ensure items are date marked after prepping and placed in a different container. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Containers storing utensils were observed to contain food and dust debris.  Discussed with PIC, utensils and containers were washed in dish machine.  Ensure containers storing food contact surfaces are cleaned regularly to prevent contamination.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Ensure all employees receive Allergen Awareness training.  Handouts given at last inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
A container of whipped cream was observed in the bar cooler without date marking.  Discussed with PIC, who corrected on-site.  Ensure items are marked properly upon opening if it will not be completely used within 24 hrs.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
A jacket was hanging on the shelf containing dry storage items.  Discussed with PIC about hanging hooks on the opposite wall of the dry storage during inspection and past inspection, or utilize the hook in the office.  Ensure personal wear items are not kept with food items to prevent contamination.

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Walk-in cooler was observed to contain an accumulation of debris and dirty towels.  Ensure the walk-in cooler floors are cleaned regularly to prevent debris and soil accumulation.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Coving tiles were observed to be missing on front line.  Discussed with PIC, spaces between wall and floor tile accumulates soil and food debris due to missing coving tiles.  Ensure tiles are replaced.

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Dish machine area caulking was observed to have cracks and places of wear.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure area is cleaned and re-caulked to prevent accumulation of moisture and mold.
-The top of the hand sinks also need to be caulked to seal the space between the sink and the wall.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Multiple holes were observed in the wall around the thermostats and around the water heater in the kitchen.  Discussed with PIC.  

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Bar hand washing sink was observed to contain a container of food.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure hand washing sinks are only used for hand washing. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Soda gun in bar was observed to contain mold and other debris.  Discussed with PIC, clean soda gun regularly to prevent contamination.  Ensure soda gun and holder are cleaned every night.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
-Containers of food in walk-in cooler were observed to be out of date.  Discussed with PIC, foods were discarded.  Ensure food is discarded after 7 days of preparation.   
-Homemade ranch dressing was observed in walk-in cooler without date marking.  Discussed with PIC, homemade dressings shall be properly labeled.  Ensure homemade dressings are properly labeled and date marked.

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Items in bar handsink at time of inspection, indicating sink was used for purpose other than handwashing. Items observed: spoon and rag. Ensure handsinks are used for handwashing only and that no items are stored in/around handsink. Bartender removed these items at time of inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Soda gun at bar observed soiled with pink slime in nozzle. Ensure soda nozzles are wash, rinsed, and sanitized nightly to avoid buildup of syrup or other debris. Bartender removed nozzle for cleaning at time of inspection.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. 

Observed a glass of water on the prep table. Ensure all employee drinks are stored at lowest possible point and away from all food prep areas. Employee drinks should also be contained in a lidded cup with a straw. Employee removed the glass from the area during inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).
*Observed can opener blade with residue. Ensure can opener is cleaned routinely to prevent contamination.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on Gallon of milk in walk-in cooler. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.
